forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred to the northeast of Tasmania extends a ridge over the southeast of the continent. This high and ridge will move eastwards over the Tasman Sea in coming days. A series of slow moving troughs will enter the west of the state today then move across the state on Wednesday and Thursday as a couple of cold fronts will move across waters to the south. A new high pressure system will become established south of the Bight during Friday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far west, extending to Eyre Peninsula and near southern coasts in the late evening. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds becoming fresh and gusty ahead of a southwest to southerly change extending across the west and about southern coasts in the afternoon and evening.

Isolated showers and thunderstorms developing across the agricultural areas, North West Pastoral and West Coast districts, becoming scattered in the far west. Maximum temperatures above average in the south and west, grading to well above above average in the north. Mostly light winds in the south, tending northeast to northwesterly in the north.

Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms possible across most districts, but remaining dry in the far northeast. Maximum temperatures below average in the west and south but above average in the northeast. Fresh and gusty north to northwesterly winds in the northeast ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change extending across all but the far northeast corner.

text.p: Isolated showers and thunderstorms over the pastoral districts. Isolated morning showers about the southern agricultural area, most likely about southern coastal districts. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh near the coast during the afternoon.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: dry in the far northeast. Generally 2 to 10 mm elsewhere but local falls of 10 to 15 mm are likely. Isolated higher totals of 15 to 25 mm possible about parts of the far west, southern coastal districts and Eyre Peninsula, particularly with thunderstorms.
